title_en: Wang Jun v. Jiangsu Qiangwei Rubber & Plastic Technology Co., Ltd. and Xuzhou Industrial Vocational and Technical College — dispute over compensation for personal injury
ruling_gist_en: Students' participation in off-campus internships arranged by schools is an extension and expansion of the school's teaching content. Both schools and enterprises bear certain obligations for safety education and management. Students' performance of practical operations related to the knowledge they have learned during off-campus internships shall not be deemed as establishing a labor relationship between students and enterprises. Injuries sustained by students during internships shall be handled as general civil tort disputes, and according to relevant tort laws, the students, schools, and enterprises shall bear corresponding liability in proportion to their respective degrees of fault.

full_text_en:
Wang Jun v. Jiangsu Qiangwei Rubber & Plastic Technology Co., Ltd. and Xuzhou Industrial Vocational and Technical College — dispute over personal injury compensation

Ruling Summary

A student's internship at an off-campus enterprise arranged by the school constitutes an extension and expansion of the school's teaching content. Both the school and the enterprise bear certain obligations for safety education and management. Where a student engages in practical operations related to the knowledge content they have learned during the off-campus internship, no labor relationship shall be deemed to exist between the student and the enterprise. Injuries sustained by the student during the internship shall be handled in accordance with the provisions on general civil tort disputes, and the student, the school, and the enterprise shall bear corresponding liability based on the degree of fault, in accordance with relevant tort laws.

Plaintiff: Wang Jun, male, Han ethnicity, 23 years old, residing in Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Jiangsu Qiangwei Rubber & Plastic Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Suyu Economic Development Zone, Suqian, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Xuzhou Industrial Vocational and Technical College, domiciled at Jiuli District, Xuzhou, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Wang Jun, filed an action with the Suyu District People's Court of Suqian, Jiangsu Province, against the defendants, Jiangsu Qiangwei Rubber & Plastic Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qiangwei Technology) and Xuzhou Industrial Vocational and Technical College (hereinafter referred to as the Vocational College), concerning a dispute over personal injury compensation.

The plaintiff, Wang Jun, alleged: The plaintiff was a student in Class 071, Rubber Specialty, Department of Engineering, of the defendant Vocational College. On December 1, 2009, the plaintiff entered the defendant Qiangwei Technology for a post-graduation internship. At approximately 3:00 p.m. on December 30, 2009, the plaintiff was injured while painting the door of the defendant's new factory building. Subsequently, the defendant Qiangwei Technology sent the plaintiff to Suqian Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine for treatment, and later transferred him to Jurong Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, where he was hospitalized for 23 days. The plaintiff was arranged by the defendant Vocational College to intern at Qiangwei Technology and was injured while working there. The two defendants should jointly compensate the plaintiff for his economic losses after the injury. The plaintiff now requests that the two defendants be ordered to pay the plaintiff RMB 134,904 in total for various losses and bear all litigation costs of this case.

The defendant Qiangwei Technology argued: The plaintiff, Wang Jun, was injured due to his own negligence and should bear the majority of the liability. There was no employment or labor relationship between our company and the plaintiff. Our company was entrusted by the Vocational College to provide internship placement for the plaintiff. This internship was an extension of the Vocational College's teaching activities. A supervising teacher should have been stationed during the internship, and general and ongoing work should have been guided by the Vocational College. Therefore, our company should not bear compensation liability to the plaintiff. The plaintiff was injured on December 30, 2009, and the plaintiff's lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations. The plaintiff's injury can no longer be verified.

The defendant Vocational College argued: It is a fact that the plaintiff, Wang Jun, was injured at the defendant Qiangwei Technology at the end of December 2009. Our college has repeatedly negotiated with Qiangwei Technology regarding compensation. At the time of the accident, the plaintiff's status had changed, and he was working at the company as an employee. From the process of the injury, the school was not at fault and should not bear liability. The school and Qiangwei Technology do not have a principal-agent relationship; the plaintiff entered Qiangwei Technology for work through a bilateral selection process. In summary, our college is not the appropriate defendant and should not bear compensation liability.

The Suyu District People's Court of Suqian found the following facts at first instance:

The plaintiff, Wang Jun, was a student in Class 071, Rubber Specialty, Department of Engineering, of the defendant Vocational College. On December 1, 2009, the defendant Vocational College uniformly arranged for graduating students to intern in accordance with Ministry of Education documents, and the plaintiff entered the defendant Qiangwei Technology for a post-graduation internship. It was agreed that the salary for the first month would be RMB 1,000, and starting from the second month, the monthly salary would be RMB 1,500. At approximately 3:00 p.m. on December 30, 2009, the plaintiff and others, arranged by Qiangwei Technology, were painting the door of the company's new factory building. Because the factory door was relatively high, the plaintiff stood on a tripod to paint the door. While moving the tripod from one side to the other, the tripod unexpectedly toppled over, causing the plaintiff, who was standing on the tripod, to fall from a height of over 2 meters and sustain injuries. After the plaintiff was injured, the defendant Qiangwei Technology sent the plaintiff to Suqian Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine for treatment, and later transferred him to Jurong Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, where he was hospitalized for 23 days. The plaintiff incurred medical expenses, lost wages, nursing fees, meal subsidies, nutrition fees, transportation fees, and other expenses totaling RMB 43,305 for medical treatment. The defendant Qiangwei Technology had already paid RMB 15,000 in medical expenses and provided 11 days of nursing care. During the litigation, upon the court's entrustment for appraisal, the plaintiff's injury was determined to constitute a Class X disability. Based on the per capita disposable income of local urban residents, the plaintiff's disability compensation amounted to RMB 45,888.

The Suyu District People's Court of Suqian held at first instance:

The plaintiff, Wang Jun, was a current student of the defendant Vocational College. He was assigned by the school to intern at Qiangwei Technology. Since this internship was an extension and expansion of the school's teaching content, the school still bore certain obligations for safety education and management regarding the plaintiff's safety at the internship unit. Qiangwei Technology, as the internship unit, had the obligation to provide the plaintiff with safety education and relevant training during the internship period, and to provide a safe workplace to ensure the plaintiff's personal safety during the internship. Since the plaintiff was interning at Qiangwei Technology to engage in practical operations related to the knowledge he had learned, there was no labor relationship between him and Qiangwei Technology. The injuries sustained by the plaintiff during the internship should be handled as a general civil tort dispute. In this case, although Qiangwei Technology, as the internship unit, provided the plaintiff with internship training, it still owed a direct duty to remind and pay attention to potential safety hazards that the plaintiff might encounter during the internship. Because Qiangwei Technology failed to fulfill this duty, it was at fault for the resulting damage of the plaintiff's injury and should bear corresponding compensation liability. The court determined this liability to be 60%, i.e., (RMB 43,305 + RMB 45,888) × 60% = RMB 53,515.8. After deducting the medical expenses already paid and 11 days of nursing fees, Qiangwei Technology should still pay RMB 53,515.8 - (RMB 15,000 + 11 × RMB 60) = RMB 37,855.8. The Vocational College failed to strengthen safety education for students and provide necessary management, thereby bearing liability for negligent management. The school was also at fault for the resulting damage of the plaintiff's injury and should bear corresponding compensation liability. The court determined this liability to be 20%, i.e., (RMB 43,305 + RMB 45,888) × 20% = RMB 17,838.6. The plaintiff, as an adult college student, also had a certain duty of care for his own safety. He did not step off the tripod while moving it during work, and was at fault for the resulting damage of his injury. Therefore, the compensation liability of the two defendants should be reduced. The court determined the plaintiff's liability to be 20%. Regarding the plaintiff's claim for moral damages, the court determined an amount of RMB 3,000, with Qiangwei Technology bearing RMB 2,000 and the Vocational College bearing RMB 1,000.

In conclusion, the Suyu District People's Court of Suqian, in accordance with Article 119 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, Articles 17 and 30 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Personal Injury Compensation, and Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment on August 17, 2011:

1. The defendant Qiangwei Technology shall pay the plaintiff Wang Jun compensation in the amount of RMB 39,855.8;
2. The defendant Vocational College shall pay the plaintiff Wang Jun compensation in the amount of RMB 18,838.6;
The above two judgments shall be performed within ten days after this judgment takes effect;
3. The plaintiff's other claims are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the Vocational College, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to the Suqian Intermediate People's Court. Subsequently, under the mediation of the Suqian Intermediate People's Court, the parties unanimously recognized the first-instance judgment result and reached the following agreement:

1. The appellant, Xuzhou Industrial Vocational and Technical College, shall pay the appellee, Wang Jun, RMB 18,838.6 before November 10, 2011;
2. The appellee, Jiangsu Qiangwei Rubber & Plastic Technology Co., Ltd., shall pay the appellee, Wang Jun, RMB 39,855.8 before November 10, 2011;
3. The first-instance case acceptance fee, reduced by half, is RMB 588, the appraisal fee is RMB 2,300, totaling RMB 2,888, to be borne by Jiangsu Qiangwei Rubber & Plastic Technology Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 2,300 and by Xuzhou Industrial Vocational and Technical College in the amount of RMB 588; the second-instance case acceptance fee, reduced by half, is RMB 588, to be borne by the appellant, Xuzhou Industrial Vocational and Technical College;
4. The parties have no other disputes in this case.

The parties unanimously agreed that this agreement shall take effect upon signing.

The Suqian Intermediate People's Court issued a civil mediation document on October 28, 2011, confirming the above agreement.
